title: Invite audit trail + granular approval policies for org/team management
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Current invite flows allow team-level invitations with a single org-wide allowlist/denylist and no consistent audit trail linking invite decisions to approvers. This causes gaps for customers with strict compliance needs: (1) administrators need per-team invite scopes and explicit org-owner approvals for cross-domain invites; (2) SSO tenants should be able to automatically block invites from unverified domains; (3) audit logs must provide immutable trails for who allowed/denied an invite and the policy used.

Goal: Implement a combined feature set that: (a) surfaces a per-team invite approval configuration (none / owner-approval / auto-allow for verified domains); (b) records structured audit events for invite decisions and policy changes, including RBAC v2 principal metadata; (c) integrates with SSO/SAML tenant settings so unverified-domain invites are elevated to approval or blocked; and (d) provides admin UI & API endpoints for exporting audit slices for compliance incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Admins can configure invite mode at org and team scope (modes: open, require-org-owner-approval, verified-domains-only, blocked)

Invite execution creates an immutable audit event with fields: actor_id, actor_role, target_email, invite_mode, decision (auto-allowed/approved/denied), policy_id, timestamp, request_ip, request_user_agent
RBAC v2 metadata (principal id, role bindings) is attached to audit events and queryable via API
SSO/SAML tenant settings include a toggle 'block_unverified_domains' that auto-blocks invites and creates an elevated incident audit event
Admin console shows per-team pending invites queue with 'approve/deny' actions and clear rationale notes
Export API returns newline-delimited JSON slices filtered by date/team/policy with retention-aware access controls
Unit and e2e tests covering policy evaluation matrix, failed/approved paths, and audit event emission exist and pass
Security review sign-off is recorded and release notes include migration instructions for customers
implementation_notes: Policy model: extend current invite policy schema to include scope (org/team), mode enum, and policy_id immutable on creation
Policy evaluation: implement short-circuit rules (blocked > owner-approval > verified-domains-only > open). Use RBAC v2 evaluator to check approver eligibility.
Audit pipeline: emit structured events to kafka topic 'audit.invites.v2' with schematized payload; tolerant backwards-compatible schema evolution required
SSO integration: when a tenant is SSO-enforced, treat tenant-verified domains as 'verified' and add auto-block rule for unverified domains if toggle set
UI: implement a per-team 'Invite settings' page with clear copy and a pending-invites tab; wire approval actions to admin service endpoints
DB migration: new tables invite_policies (id, org_id, team_id nullable, mode, created_by, created_at) and invite_audit_events (id, invite_id, payload_json) using elastic retention policy
Rate limiting: approval endpoints must be throttled and protected by admin-only RBAC v2 guardrails
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): API + audit emission only for 10% of orgs; no UI changes; validate schema and retention behavior
Phase 2 (opt-in): Expose team invite settings in console behind feature flag; selected enterprise customers switch to owner-approval for testing
Phase 3 (enforcement): Enable enforcement for orgs with 'security_profile=strict'; migrate existing org-level allowlist/denylist into new policy object with admin notification
Phase 4 (public): Default new orgs to 'verified-domains-only' for SSO tenants and document migration path for older orgs
Rollback: turn off enforcement flag and backfill denial events as notes; audit schema is append-only so no deletion required for rollback
qa_checks: Simulate invites from verified and unverified domains under SSO tenant and confirm decisions and audit payloads
Run RBAC v2 matrix tests: org-owner, team-admin, regular-member attempting approvals
Verify console pending-invites queue shows correct metadata and action buttons for admin roles
Export slice for a week and validate NDJSON format, size, and fields mapping to spec
Pen-test invite approval endpoints for parameter tampering and privilege escalation
risks: False positives: overzealous blocking could cause customer-reported outages for invite flows; mitigate with gradual rollout and easy admin bypass
Schema drift: audit schema changes may break downstream SIEM ingestion; mitigate with strict schema registry and consumer contracts
Performance: per-invite policy evaluation could add latency on high-throughput orgs; mitigate with caching of evaluated team policies and preflight checks
Data retention/compliance: audit logs contain PII (emails) — ensure encryption-at-rest and access controls; coordinate with legal
SSO edge cases: third-party IdPs with delayed domain verification may cause invites to be blocked; provide manual override pathway and clear UX messaging
